topic: First modern Olympic Games: Athens, 6–15 April 1896, opened in the Panathenaic Stadium (ancient stadium rebuilt in white marble, paid for by Georgios Averoff); 241 athletes from 14 nations, 43 events, all male; first women at Paris 1900 (22 women). First champion James Connolly (USA), triple jump, 6 April 1896, who had left Harvard to compete. Marathon (first ever) ≈ 40 km from Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium, 10 April 1896, won by Spyridon Louis, a Greek water carrier, in 2:58:50.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The modern Olympics began in Paris, home of their founder Pierre de Coubertin.
myths.reality: Coubertin founded the IOC in Paris in 1894, but the first Games were held in Athens in April 1896; Paris hosted the second Games in 1900.
